title: Global market share of three computer operating systems - Pie Chart

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the global market share of three computer operating systems and other systems from 2012 to 2015.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, OS 1 experienced substantial growth throughout the period while Others showed a dramatic decline. By the end of the period, OS 1 had become the dominant operating system, capturing more than half of the market.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the most dramatically changing categories, in 2012, Others held the largest market share at 48%, which was more than double that of OS 1 at 20%. However, OS 1 underwent remarkable expansion over the four-year period, surging to 38% in 2013, then to 47% in 2014, before reaching its peak of 52% in 2015. In contrast, Others experienced a precipitous decline, plummeting from nearly half of the market to 35% in 2013, then continuing its downward trajectory to 23% in 2014 and finally reaching a mere 15% by 2015.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the more stable operating systems, OS 2 maintained a relatively consistent market share throughout the period, starting at 17% in 2012 and remaining at this level in 2013, before showing a marginal increase to 18% in both 2014 and 2015. Similarly, OS 3 demonstrated limited variation, beginning at 15% in 2012, dropping to its lowest point of 10% in 2013, then recovering slightly to 12% in 2014 before returning to 15% in the final year.
